Reaction in solution  
Ca²⁺  +  EDTA⁴⁻  ⇌  Ca-EDTA²⁻  β = Kf = 5×10¹⁰

Let  
[Ca-EDTA²⁻]₀ = 0.020 M (the given stoichiometric concentration).  
When a small amount x of the complex dissociates,

Ca-EDTA²⁻  →  Ca²⁺  +  EDTA⁴⁻  

Equilibrium concentrations  
[Ca-EDTA²⁻]   = 0.020 – x  
[Ca²⁺]        = x  
[EDTA⁴⁻]       = x  

Insert these in the formation-constant expression:

β = [Ca-EDTA²⁻]/([Ca²⁺][EDTA⁴⁻])  
5×10¹⁰ = (0.020 – x)/(x·x)

Because β is very large, only a minute fraction dissociates, so x ≪ 0.020 M and 0.020 – x ≈ 0.020 M:

x² ≈ 0.020 / (5×10¹⁰)  
x² ≈ 4×10⁻¹³  
x ≈ √(4×10⁻¹³) ≈ 6.3×10⁻⁷ M

Thus the concentration of free Ca²⁺ ions is about 6.3×10⁻⁷ M.

(A) 2.0×10⁻² M  
(B) 1.0×10⁻² M  
(C) 5.0×10⁻³ M  
(D) 6.3×10⁻⁷ M  ← correct

Answer: D
